questions.question: Why must large food molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats be digested?
options: To allow them to be converted directly into water.
To break them down into smaller molecules that can be absorbed by the body.
To convert them into toxic substances that the body can easily excrete.
To build them into larger structures before they enter the bloodstream.

questions.question: How are absorbed nutrients transported to the cells where they are needed?
options: Through the lymphatic system only
Through the nervous system
Through the blood
Through the digestive tract itself

questions.question: By what process do small, soluble nutrient molecules pass directly into the blood?
options: Diffusion
Active filtration
Osmotic suction
Condensation

questions.question: Which of the following is an adaptation of the small intestine lining that increases the absorption of nutrients?
options: A thick layer of muscular tissue that slows down food movement
A very small surface area to concentrate the nutrients
Microvilli and villi that greatly increase the surface area
A smooth, waterproof lining that prevents liquids from escaping

questions.question: What is a bacterium?
options: A non-living chemical compound found in digestive juices
A multicellular fungus that decomposes food
A microscopic living organism made of a single cell
A virus that only lives inside animal cells

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of bacteria in relation to human health?
options: All bacteria are harmful pathogens that cause diseases.
All bacteria are completely harmless to humans.
Some bacteria cause diseases, but many are harmless and some are helpful.
Bacteria can only survive outside the human body.

questions.question: Where in the human body do helpful bacteria live to assist with digestive processes?
options: Inside the lungs
Inside the digestive system
Inside the kidneys
Inside the heart muscle

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria in our digestive system help us digest food that we cannot break down ourselves?
options: They produce acid that dissolves the food.
They physically chew the food inside the intestines.
They release enzymes that break down these foods.
They absorb the food whole and destroy it.

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria protect us from harmful pathogens in the digestive system?
options: By competing against them
By producing white blood cells
By raising the temperature of the gut
By building physical walls around them

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a type of digestion with its description and location?
options: Chemical digestion involves physical churning in the mouth only.
Mechanical digestion involves enzymes breaking bonds, which occurs in the blood.
Mechanical digestion physically breaks food into smaller pieces (e.g., chewing in the mouth), while chemical digestion uses enzymes to break chemical bonds (e.g., in the stomach and small intestine).
Both mechanical and chemical digestion refer only to the action of stomach acid.

questions.question: What are the three main groups of large molecules that make up the food we eat?
options: Minerals, vitamins, and water
Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
Sugars, amino acids, and lactic acid
Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen

questions.question: What is the main role of enzymes in chemical digestion?
options: To act as biological catalysts that speed up the breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
To provide energy to the muscle walls of the stomach
To physically grind food into smaller particles in the mouth
To transport nutrients from the small intestine to the liver

questions.question: What are proteins broken down into during chemical digestion?
options: Fatty acids and glycerol
Amino acids
Starch and simple sugars
Water and mineral salts

questions.question: Which chemical reagent is commonly used to test for the presence of the large carbohydrate starch?
options: Ethanol
Iodine solution
Biuret reagent
Benedict's solution

questions.question: Which reagent is used to test for small sugar molecules resulting from the breakdown of starch?
options: Iodine solution
Benedict's reagent
Biuret reagent
Ethanol emulsion

questions.question: If a food sample is tested with Biuret reagent and the colour changes from blue to purple, what does this qualitative result indicate?
options: The presence of starch
The presence of lipids (fats)
The presence of sugar
The presence of protein

questions.question: Which of the following lists the major organs of the digestive system in the correct order that food passes through them?
options: Mouth -> Stomach -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine
Mouth -> Large Intestine -> Stomach -> Small Intestine
Stomach -> Mouth -> Large Intestine -> Small Intestine
Mouth -> Small Intestine -> Stomach -> Large Intestine

questions.question: What is a major function of the stomach in the digestive system?
options: To absorb water and solidify waste into faeces
To release bile to emulsify fats
To churn food and release acidic gastric juices to begin protein digestion
To absorb digested nutrients directly into the brain

questions.question: What happens to food material that cannot be digested by the human body?
options: It is completely dissolved into gas and exhaled.
It is absorbed into the bloodstream and stored in bones.
It is passed out of the body as faeces.
It is converted into urine by the kidneys.
